sources.title: UNESCO: Mbanza Kongo, capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo
sources.note: Outstanding Universal Value: capital, stone building, customary institutions and living traditions.

sources.title: South African History Online: Kingdom of Kongo
sources.note: Historical synthesis with academic references; civil war, restoration, changing nineteenth-century economy and colonial incorporation.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Kongo textiles in Renaissance European collections
sources.note: Raffia techniques, geometric designs and seventeenth-century collection records.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Kongo Christian art
sources.note: Sixteenth- to seventeenth-century brass crucifix 1999.295.7 and local textile imagery.

sources.title: Mbelolo Ya Mpiko: The 1624 Kikongo catechism and intercultural communication
sources.note: Four-page academic conference paper. Semantic discussion explicitly gives the historical form zambiampungu and its Christian and ancestral meanings.

sources.title: Jelmer Vos: Empire, patronage and a revolt in the kingdom of Kongo
sources.note: Cadernos de Estudos Africanos 33 (2017), pages 157 to 182. Forced recruitment, reciprocal obligations and the 1913 revolt. Some PDF numerals have faulty text encoding.

sources.title: Alisa LaGamma: The recently acquired Kongo Mangaaka power figure
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum Journal 43 (2008). Nineteenth-century regional Kongo ritual objects; not assumed to originate in the mapped kingdom.

sources.title: Republic of the Congo: initial report to the Committee on the Rights of the Child
sources.note: Historical section, paragraphs 33 to 34: 1958 reorganization, independence, one-party government and 1991 conference. State report, used for dated events rather than claims of democratic quality.

sources.title: Cambridge: Chinese railroad workers in French Congo
sources.note: Historical study of labour on the Congo-Océan railway; construction, coercion and mortality.

sources.title: UNESCO Brazzaville: Poto-Poto painting exhibition, March 2023
sources.note: School founded in 1951; named painter Marcel Gotène; intergenerational exhibition and 2002 Picasso medal.

sources.title: UNESCO: Congolese rumba
sources.note: Joint Republic of the Congo and DRC inscription, 2021; social settings, women musicians, apprenticeship and instrument making.

sources.title: UNICEF Congo: Finally, water at school
sources.note: 23 August 2022; named Pointe-Noire primary school, water point, parents and pupil-led hygiene clubs.

sources.title: UNICEF Congo: The school canteen
sources.note: 31 August 2021; Bernadette Bayonne school in Brazzaville, mothers preparing meals and handwashing facilities.

sources.title: Republic of the Congo: Constitution of 25 October 2015
sources.note: Original French, articles 1 to 4; capital, motto, French official language and Lingala/Kituba vehicular languages.

sources.title: South African History Online: Zulu
sources.note: Household work, late eighteenth-century political consolidation and colonial-era taxes, crop loss and cattle disease.

sources.title: Franco Frescura: Culture in transition, lecture 2
sources.note: Architectural study of southern African homesteads, circular Nguni layout and central cattle byre. Regional pattern, not a universal floor plan.

sources.title: National Army Museum: Zulu War
sources.note: British invasion, Cetshwayo, Isandlwana and Ulundi. Avoid the page’s disputed casualty totals.

sources.title: John Laband: Historical Dictionary of the Zulu Wars
sources.note: Entries Zululand, British Colony of and Zululand, Province of; 1887 annexation, hut taxes and 1897 incorporation.

sources.title: British Museum: Zulu headrest Af.577
sources.note: Carved wooden headrest made before 1865; four legs, pokerwork and dimensions.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Lidded prestige vessel, circle of Unobadula
sources.note: Object 2013.165a,b; mid to late nineteenth century; one-block carving, clients, 1862 exhibition and uncertain function.

sources.title: National Library of South Africa: Ilanga lase Natal
sources.note: Digitized newspaper collection; John Dube, April 1903 foundation, place of publication and language history.

sources.title: Stellenbosch University ESAT: Ilanga lase Natal
sources.note: Title translated as The Natal Sun; isiZulu newspaper founded in 1903.

sources.title: National Museums Scotland: The British raid on Benin, 1897
sources.note: Conquest, removal of royal objects and later museum acquisitions.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Head of an oba, 1977.187.37
sources.note: Brass and iron ancestral head; metadata says nineteenth century while essay proposes late eighteenth century. Card preserves approximate late dating rather than resolving this discrepancy.

sources.title: Kathy Curnow: The Bright Continent, Kingdom-based art
sources.note: Benin section: court hierarchy, late palace changes and Eweka’s 1914 restoration and rebuilding.

sources.title: MOWAA team: Benin City archaeology and urban development
sources.note: Antiquity 100, issue 409 (2026), e11; first online 2025. Fieldwork 2022 to 2024; pottery, workshop, plants and shrine interpretation.

sources.title: British Museum and MOWAA: Archaeology Project in Benin City
sources.note: About the project: precolonial habitation areas, wells, cisterns and workshops, young Nigerian archaeologists and community engagement.

sources.title: Centre for Edo Studies: Egharevba autobiography, chapter 10
sources.note: Edo text with page images; names Ekhere vb’ Itan Ẹdo, publication in January 1933 and English version A Short History of Benin.

sources.title: Usuanlele and Falola: The Scholarship of Jacob Egharevba of Benin
sources.note: History in Africa 21 (1994), article extract. Family trading, schooling, 1921 draft, 1933 publication and subsequent English translation.

sources.title: Government of Benin: History
sources.note: Colony established in 1894, independence in 1960, 1975 name change and 1990 National Conference. Promotional assessments of contemporary democracy are not repeated.

sources.title: National Archives of Benin: Recent holdings
sources.note: Dated postcolonial archival periods: 1960 to 1972, 1972 to 1990 and post-1991.

sources.title: UNESCO: Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba
sources.note: Benin and Togo living landscape; tower-house construction, animal spaces, terrace granaries and rebuilding.

sources.title: UNESCO: Oral heritage of Gelede
sources.note: Yoruba-Nago communities in Benin, Nigeria and Togo; ceremony, carving, costume preparation and satirical poetry.

sources.title: Benin nomination: Lower Ouémé Valley
sources.note: 2020 state submission to UNESCO Tentative List; Tofin and Ouémè stilt villages, seasonal flooding, fishing and farming. It is not a World Heritage inscription.

sources.title: Benin: Constitution of 11 December 1990
sources.note: Original French constitutional text, article 1; motto and symbols. Historical 1990 text, not legal advice about later amendments.

sources.title: National Archives of Tunisia: Historical overview
sources.note: Husainid dynasty from 1705; nineteenth-century reforms and archive service founded in 1874.

sources.title: Museum With No Frontiers: Hammuda Pasha Mosque
sources.note: Mohamed Béji Ben Mami. Muradid monument dated by inscription to 1655; prayer hall, courtyard and funerary architecture.

sources.title: Tunisian National Heritage Institute: Presentation of Tunisian museums
sources.note: Dar Ben Abdallah section: reconstructed domestic scenes, nineteenth-century women’s work, kitchen and wedding objects. Reconstructions are identified as such.

sources.title: University of Florence: Dar Ben Abdallah museum and popular memory
sources.note: 2022 architectural study; eighteenth-century residence and museum presentation of nineteenth- and twentieth-century upper-middle-class Tunisian life.

sources.title: National Archives of Tunisia: Constitution of 1861
sources.note: Primary constitutional text in French translation; chapter I, hereditary succession and family registers.

sources.title: Tunisian Ministry of Justice: Fundamental Pact of 1857
sources.note: Arabic excerpt of article 1; guarantees for inhabitants across religions, languages and colours, plus tax/trade provisions. The quoted phrase is reproduced from the ministry’s transcription.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France: Tunisia under the French protectorate
sources.note: Historical authority record: 1881 invasion and Bardo treaty, 1883 convention, independence in 1956.

sources.title: Tunisian government: Discover Tunisia
sources.note: Dates for protectorate, independence 20 March 1956 and republic 25 July 1957.

sources.title: UNESCO: Pottery skills of the women of Sejnane
sources.note: 2018 inscription; clay processing, household wares and toys, family learning and adaptation.

sources.title: Tunisian National Heritage Institute: Sejnane inventory for UNESCO
sources.note: French inventory identifies potter Halima Saïdani and her daughter Hajer, aged 17 at documentation, combining school and craft.

sources.title: UNESCO: Harissa knowledge and culinary practices
sources.note: 2022 inscription; household preparation, ingredients, tools, storage and agricultural teaching.

sources.title: UNESCO: Djerba settlement pattern
sources.note: 2023 inscription; family estates, neighbourhoods, mixed communities, defensive buildings and modern changes.

sources.title: Constitute: Tunisia’s 2014 constitution, original Arabic
sources.note: Historical text; preamble dates the revolution and article 4 gives the motto.

sources.title: Tunisia: Constitution of 17 August 2022
sources.note: Official constitutional text reproduced in the Tunisian legal database. Used to distinguish the 2014 document from the later constitution.

sources.title: US Department of State: Libya historical background, 2007 archive
sources.note: Historical events only: 1934 colony, 1943 to 1951 administrations, 1951 independence, 1959 oil and 1969 coup. No then-current political claims reused.

sources.title: Ali Abdullatif Ahmida: Genocide in colonial Libya, 1929 to 1934
sources.note: Cambridge World History of Genocide, 2023, chapter 5. Scholarly interpretation of deportation, camps, resistance and suppressed memory; no disputed precise casualty estimate reproduced.

sources.title: Libya: Constitution of 1951, Arabic text in DCAF Legal Database
sources.note: Primary historical text, articles 1, 2, 3, 28 to 30; original writing, federal monarchy and education provisions.

sources.title: UNESCO: Old Town of Ghadamès
sources.note: Domestic levels, terraces, covered streets, water management, traditional materials and present use without permanent residence.

sources.title: NASA Earth Observatory: Water Beneath the Sand
sources.note: 2023 satellite-based discussion of Kufrah, ancient groundwater and pipelines to coastal cities.

sources.title: UNICEF: Libya Storm Daniel situation report, November 2023
sources.note: Restoration of schools, primary care and water/sanitation after the September 2023 floods.

sources.title: UNESCO: Safeguarding manuscripts in Libya
sources.note: 2019 account, updated 2023; Benghazi University manuscripts recovered in 2017, classification and digitization.

sources.title: United Nations: Special Representative’s briefing on Libya, 20 October 2011
sources.note: Contemporaneous report of Qadhafi’s death and the transition after his rule.

sources.title: UNSMIL: Independence Day statement, 24 December 2023
sources.note: 72nd independence anniversary and elections that were not held in December 2021. Dated account, not prediction or unverified current election status.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Decoded border features are in northern Angola around Mbanza Kongo: congo 1492 to 1878; congo-1900 1900 to 1914. Shared narrative covers the independent kingdom and dependent colonial phase. Do not identify either polygon as the Congo Free State or Republic of the Congo. Imported gaps and outlines retained; no claim that 1914 was a clean extinction of kingship.

Decoded polygon [11.15,-5,18.56,3.53] matches Congo-Brazzaville, not DRC or Kongo. Index 1945 to present crosses French Middle Congo and independence in 1960; narrative explicitly dates that transition.

Adjacent southern African polygons refer to the kingdom and its conquered region. zulu 1783 to 1878 predates Shaka at its start; zululand 1878 to 1914 spans 1879 conquest, 1887 colony and 1897 Natal incorporation. Shared phase narrative explicitly avoids portraying a sovereign kingdom throughout both intervals.

Polygon [4.64,4.96,6.1,6.29] is Edo Benin in Nigeria. Existing older benin card untouched. Imported endpoint 1914 intersects royal restoration, not disappearance. Modern benin-1945 is a different country.

Polygon [.84,6.25,3.83,12.34] matches modern Benin. Index 1945 to present spans colonial Dahomey, independence 1960, name change 1975 and 1990 transition. Not the Edo kingdom; existing dahomey and benin cards left untouched.

Index 1650 to 1878; Tunis-area features inspected at 1715, 1800, 1815 and 1878. Narrative spans Muradid and Husainid phases; 1878 is an imported cutoff, not the historical end. Protectorate begins 1881.

Index 1900 to present crosses French protectorate, 1956 independence and 1957 republic. Decoded features include 1900 to 1914, 1914 to 1945 and 1960 onward; imported 1945 to 1960 geometry gap is not interpreted as the country ceasing to exist.

Index begins 1938 and continues to present, but imported geometry is observed at 1938 to 1945 and 1960 onward. It crosses Italian colonial, Allied occupation, independent kingdom and later phases. Narrative does not treat gaps as disappearance or claim a present unified administration.
